The report mentioned that during Zhu Rongji's serious illness, leaders including Xi Jinping and Li Qiang visited him in hospital; after his death, they also expressed deep condolences in various forms and extended their sympathies to his family. Xinhua's first report on Zhu Rongji's farewell ceremony did not include photos from the event; photos of Xi Jinping shaking hands with Zhu Rongji's family members were only added in subsequent updates.

Additionally, during Zhu Rongji's farewell ceremony, security measures in Beijing were tightened compared to those during Li Keqiang's funeral. According to reports from Reuters, Taiwan's Central News Agency and EBC News, shortly after 8 a.m., a hearse believed to be carrying Zhu Rongji's body appeared near Tiananmen Square, heading towards Babaoshan.

Members of the public were unable to wave goodbye to the hearse from the roadside

Traffic control was implemented along the route from Tiananmen to Babaoshan from around 7 a.m., with multiple police vehicles and plainclothes personnel stationed at various locations. At Babaoshan station where the farewell ceremony was held, controls were enforced in the morning. Within several kilometres near Babaoshan, not only were SWAT vehicles parked on the roads, but large numbers of plainclothes personnel dressed in black were stationed on streets and pedestrian footbridges, making it difficult for pedestrians to gather or stop by the roadside. The plainclothes officers also dispersed members of the public lingering on the road, and the blockade was not lifted until around 10 a.m. Members of the public, unlike on the day of Li Keqiang's cremation, were unable to stand by the roadside and wave to the hearse as it travelled to Babaoshan. Instead, citizens could only leave condolence messages online. In the comment sections of Xinhua News Agency and CCTV reports, large numbers of internet users posted messages of mourning, including "Premier Zhu, have a safe journey" and "Deeply mourn," or used images of small candles to express their condolences.

Although the public found it difficult to bid farewell along the route, the authorities arranged for flags to be flown at half-mast at Tiananmen Square in Beijing on the morning of his cremation day. Important institutions in Beijing, including Xinhua Gate, the Great Hall of the People and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, also flew flags at half-mast. Government headquarters, Government House and airport entry and exit ports in Hong Kong and Macau also flew flags at half-mast in mourning for Zhu Rongji.

"Iron-faced Premier," "Economic Tsar"

Looking back on Zhu Rongji's life, beyond titles such as "Iron-faced Premier" and "Economic Tsar," he was witty and eloquent. During his state visit to the United States in 1999, he appeared alongside former US President Bill Clinton at a joint press conference, taking questions from international media on issues including China-US relations, human rights and Taiwan, leaving a deep impression on the outside world.

"Without hesitation, giving everything until my last breath"

Zhu Rongji also left behind many memorable quotes during his tenure. After succeeding Li Peng as Premier at the Two Sessions in 1998, he said at his first press conference with Chinese and foreign journalists: "Whether there is a minefield ahead or an abyss, I will forge ahead without retreat, without hesitation, giving everything until my last breath." To demonstrate his determination to fight corruption, he once declared: "I have prepared 100 coffins — 99 for corrupt officials and one for myself." Even the term "tofu-dreg projects" (豆腐渣工程) was coined by him during his inspection of flood-stricken areas in Jiangxi in 1998.

Reading two Hong Kong newspapers every day — Zhu Rongji's long-standing concern for Hong Kong also made him one of the national leaders most familiar with the city. His connection with Hong Kong began as early as 1990, when he served as Mayor of Shanghai. That year, he led an economic and trade delegation on a visit to Hong Kong, and went on to visit the city four times before his retirement. He also paid close attention to developments in Hong Kong, reading two Hong Kong newspapers every day to keep abreast of the latest situation.

"If Hong Kong is not run well..."

The Selected Works of Zhu Rongji's Speeches (《朱鎔基講話實錄》), published by People's Publishing House in 2011, compiles many of Zhu Rongji's important speeches, including his 22-minute address at the welcome banquet held at Government House during his visit to Hong Kong in late 2002. When discussing Hong Kong's governance and future, he said: "The future of Hong Kong is bright, and we will always be proud of Hong Kong. I do not believe Hong Kong cannot be run well. If Hong Kong is not run well, it is not only your responsibility, but also ours. If Hong Kong's return to the motherland fails under our watch, would we not have become sinners of the nation? That will not happen."

Zhu Rongji also expressed support on multiple occasions for Hong Kong to maintain its linked exchange rate system. During the Asian Financial Crisis, when the Hong Kong dollar came under attack from international speculators including the famous George Soros, Zhu Rongji declared publicly that he would "spare no effort to safeguard Hong Kong's prosperity and stability and protect its linked exchange rate system".

As early as his tenure as Vice Premier, Zhu Rongji had already openly supported Hong Kong's linked exchange rate system. In December 1997, he met with representatives at the meeting of general managers of overseas branches of the Bank of China and the People's Insurance Company (Group) of China, and delivered a speech titled "Drawing Lessons Seriously from the Asian Financial Crisis".

He stated that "Hong Kong successfully maintained its linked exchange rate system by itself," and added: "Do not criticise Hong Kong's linked exchange rate system... We should only support all measures taken by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government... At this critical moment, with the enemy at the gate, we must not criticise but only offer support and encouragement."

Zhu Rongji also noted at the time that compared with other Southeast Asian countries and regions, Hong Kong's financial system was relatively sound. The problem of Hong Kong's property market, unlike in countries such as Thailand, was not due to oversupply but rather to excessively high land prices driving up property prices. Therefore, the speculative bubble component in Hong Kong's economy was relatively small, and he expressed full confidence in Hong Kong's future.
